channel.title: PsyDigest — psychiatry literature digest
channel.description: Summaries of new psychiatric research and guidelines

item.title: Pharmacotherapy for social anxiety disorder: An evidence-based treatment review.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This narrative review addresses pharmacologic treatments for social anxiety disorder (SAD), a common and often chronic condition, by synthesizing evidence from randomized controlled trials, open-label studies, and guidelines to guide treatment decisions across medication classes and emerging interventions.
FINDINGS: SSRIs and SNRIs are supported as first-line pharmacotherapies for SAD based on available evidence. For patients with incomplete response, switching within or across antidepressant classes and combining pharmacotherapy with behavioral interventions is recommended. Additional options such as benzodiazepines, monoamine oxidase inhibitors, pregabalin, and selected augmentation strategies may be considered, though the evidence is more limited. Data on long-term outcomes and treatment-resistant populations remain sparse.
INTERPRETATION: As a narrative review, this study synthesizes existing evidence rather than generating new data, and its conclusions are based on a qualitative assessment of heterogeneous studies. The strength of evidence varies significantly across medication classes, with robust support for SSRIs/SNRIs but more limited data for alternatives. The review highlights important gaps, particularly regarding long-term outcomes and treatment-resistant SAD, which limit the ability to make definitive recommendations. The lack of quantitative effect sizes or direct comparisons between treatments further constrains the interpretation.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: SSRIs and SNRIs remain the cornerstone of pharmacologic treatment for SAD, with individualized sequencing and integration with behavioral interventions recommended for partial responders. Clinicians should be cautious when considering alternatives due to limited evidence, and prioritize long-term management strategies given the chronic nature of SAD. Further research is needed to clarify optimal treatment strategies for resistant cases.

item.title: Autistic Masking and Mental Health Outcomes in Autistic Women: A Systematic Review (2015-2025).
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review (2015–2025) asked whether autistic masking—strategies to conceal autistic traits—worsens anxiety, depression, autistic burnout, or suicidality in formally diagnosed autistic adult women, and which masking measures best predict these outcomes.
FINDINGS: Nine cross-sectional and cohort studies (>1,500 women across seven countries) showed consistent associations: masking with anxiety (β = 0.21–0.22; d = 0.93) and depression (g = 0.56; Nagelkerke R² = 0.358 for lifetime diagnosis), and an independent link to suicidality (β = 0.198; OR ≈ 5 vs. general population). The CAT-Q assimilation subscale predicted suicidal ideation via anxiety. No study measured autistic burnout with validated tools.
INTERPRETATION: Evidence is moderate in strength (mostly observational, heterogeneous measures) but points to masking as a clinically meaningful psychosocial risk factor. Effect sizes for anxiety and depression are moderate-to-large, while the suicidality association, though strong, is based on a small subset of studies and indirect comparisons. Key limitations include lack of longitudinal data, validated burnout assessment, and standardized masking instruments.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Routine clinical assessment should include validated masking scales (e.g., CAT-Q) and targeted suicide-risk evaluation in autistic women, especially those reporting high assimilation demands. Further longitudinal research is needed to determine whether reducing masking causally improves mental health outcomes.

item.title: Antipsychotic-Induced Remodeling of the Gut Microbiota: Drug-Specific Patterns and Molecular Links to Metabolic Adverse Effects.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This structured narrative review examines how antipsychotic drugs (used for schizophrenia-spectrum and severe psychiatric disorders) alter the gut microbiota and whether these changes contribute to metabolic adverse effects such as weight gain and inflammation. It synthesizes human, animal, and in vitro evidence to identify drug-specific patterns and molecular pathways linking antipsychotics to microbiota-mediated metabolic effects.
FINDINGS: Olanzapine shows the strongest evidence, with germ-free, antibiotic-depletion, and colonization studies supporting microbiota-dependent contributions to weight gain, adiposity, inflammation, and lipid dysregulation. Risperidone also demonstrates microbiota-dependent metabolic and neurobiological effects, while evidence for clozapine, quetiapine, aripiprazole, lurasidone, and amisulpride is more heterogeneous or limited. Functional pathways (e.g., short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, immune signaling) appear more informative than specific bacterial taxa.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence is largely preclinical with methodological heterogeneity, small human cohorts, and confounding, limiting causal inference. While olanzapine and risperidone show consistent microbiota-mediated metabolic effects in controlled studies, findings for other antipsychotics are inconsistent or preliminary. The review highlights plausible biological mechanisms but cannot yet determine clinical significance or guide treatment choices based on microbiota modulation.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current evidence does not support microbiome-based antipsychotic selection or adjunctive microbiome-targeted interventions in routine care. Future longitudinal multi-omic studies in treatment-naive patients are needed before considering microbiota modulation as a strategy to mitigate metabolic adverse effects.

item.title: Autistic burnout: Early insights from a systematic review on characteristics, precipitating factors, and protective mechanisms.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: Autistic burnout is an understudied phenomenon with limited professional awareness despite advocacy from autistic individuals. This systematic review synthesizes early research on its characteristics, precipitating factors, recovery strategies, and distinctions from depression, using PRISMA guidelines and qualitative analysis of 13 studies.
FINDINGS: The review identified 13 studies describing autistic burnout as involving mental/physical exhaustion, cognitive impairment (especially executive dysfunction), and severe mental health impacts (e.g., self-injury, suicidal ideation). Precipitating factors included masking, social demands, and chronic stressors. Recovery often involved self-awareness, support from autistic communities, and targeted interventions, though some individuals reported incomplete recovery.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence is preliminary and heterogeneous, based on a small, qualitative literature with variable study quality (assessed via CASP checklists). The distinction from depression remains unclear, and representativeness is limited. The findings highlight a critical gap in clinical knowledge but cannot yet guide definitive practice changes due to methodological limitations and lack of quantitative data.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Clinicians should recognize autistic burnout as a distinct, potentially severe condition with overlapping features to depression, particularly in autistic adults experiencing chronic stress or masking. Further research is needed before specific recommendations can be made; meanwhile, validating patient experiences and avoiding misdiagnosis (e.g., as solely depression) may improve care.

item.title: Multimodal Machine Learning Approaches to Detect Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) Using Physiological and Behavioural Biomarkers: A Systematic Review.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review (PRISMA 2020) examined whether multimodal machine learning (ML) or deep learning (DL) approaches using physiological and behavioural biomarkers can improve detection of ADHD, a common neurodevelopmental disorder. The review synthesised 25 heterogeneous studies published 2015–2026 that combined neuroimaging, EEG, HRV, EDA, behavioural assessments, and wearable/IoT data to classify ADHD.
FINDINGS: Included studies varied widely in design and sample size (n = 22 to 15,883; mostly cross-sectional). Early multimodal fusion models often reported diagnostic accuracies above 80%, with candidate biomarkers including frontal brain activity, heart rate patterns, and oculomotor behaviour. However, substantial differences in data sources, acquisition, feature extraction, modelling, and evaluation protocols precluded direct comparison and raised concerns about generalisability and reliability.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is preliminary and heterogeneous, with small and often unrepresentative samples and inconsistent methodological standards. While reported accuracies are promising, the lack of standardised protocols, leakage-safe validation, and multi-site testing limits internal and external validity. Model interpretability and real-world clinical applicability remain uncertain. Stronger, standardised evidence is needed before these tools can be recommended for routine ADHD assessment.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current multimodal ML/DL approaches are not yet ready for bedside use in ADHD diagnosis. Clinicians should await larger, multi-site, standardised studies with transparent validation before considering adoption; meanwhile, standard clinical assessment remains the gold standard.

item.title: Effects of ADHD Medications on Male Reproductive Function: A Systematic Review of In Vivo Mammalian Evidence.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review examined controlled in vivo mammalian studies on the effects of ADHD medications (methylphenidate, clonidine, lisdexamfetamine) on male reproductive outcomes, addressing concerns about long-term use before reproductive maturity. The review synthesised evidence on consistency, timing, reversibility, and certainty of associations.
FINDINGS: Twenty-two studies were included (19 methylphenidate, 2 clonidine, 1 lisdexamfetamine), primarily in rats (n=17), with few in mice (n=4) or rhesus macaques (n=1). During active methylphenidate exposure, adverse effects were frequently reported on spermatogenesis, sperm quantity/quality, testicular microstructure, testosterone, and inflammatory markers. Post-exposure findings were often neutral or partially reversible. Clonidine studies suggested altered epididymal contractility, while the single lisdexamfetamine study reported broad adverse effects. All 18 drug-by-outcome domains were rated as very low certainty due to small samples, heterogeneity, unclear risk of bias, and indirectness to human therapeutic use.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence is preliminary and inconsistent, with no high or moderate certainty findings. The animal models, dosing, and exposure durations are not directly comparable to clinical ADHD treatment in humans. While signals of potential reproductive toxicity exist—particularly during active exposure—quantitative risk estimation is not possible. The review highlights critical gaps, including lack of replication, incomplete reporting, and indirectness.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current evidence does not justify changes to clinical practice regarding ADHD medication use in males of reproductive age. Clinicians should remain aware of theoretical concerns but prioritise evidence from human studies. Further research—particularly prospective human cohorts—is needed before any risk assessment can be made.

item.title: ''Not a Universal Effect'': Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids and Cognition from Pregnancy to Adolescence-A Narrative Review and Nutritional Guidance for a Mediterranean Population.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This narrative review examines whether polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), particularly docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) and eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), improve cognitive outcomes from pregnancy through adolescence, synthesizing human and animal studies without a systematic search protocol. The focus is on Mediterranean populations, especially Lebanon, and includes genetic influences on PUFA metabolism.
FINDINGS: Animal models consistently show neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory effects of omega-3 PUFAs during critical brain development windows. Human studies, however, show inconsistent cognitive benefits, with potential benefits more pronounced in populations with low baseline PUFA status, learning difficulties, ADHD, or preterm birth. Genetic variants in FADS1, FADS2, and ELOVL2/5 influence long-chain PUFA synthesis and may explain variability in response to supplementation.
INTERPRETATION: As a narrative review without systematic screening, this study is limited by selection bias and lack of rigorous quality assessment of included studies. The evidence on cognitive benefits in humans is preliminary and heterogeneous, with stronger signals in specific subgroups rather than the general population. Genetic factors add complexity but are not yet actionable in routine care. The review provides useful context but does not establish causality or quantify effect sizes for clinical decision-making.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current evidence does not support routine omega-3 supplementation for cognitive enhancement in Mediterranean populations. Focus should remain on improving adherence to traditional Mediterranean diets rich in PUFAs. Clinicians should consider targeted supplementation in high-risk groups (e.g., preterm infants, ADHD) but await stronger evidence before changing practice.

item.title: Predicting cognitive-behavioral therapy outcomes in obsessive-compulsive disorder from inhibitory control neural activity: A mega-analysis and machine learning study from the ENIGMA-OCD consortium.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This mega-analysis and machine learning study from the ENIGMA-OCD consortium (n=130, age 8–57, 54% female) examined whether pre-treatment fMRI activity during inhibitory control and error processing tasks could predict cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) outcomes in obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD).
FINDINGS: Remission after CBT was associated with weaker activity in default mode regions during response inhibition and in the right supramarginal gyrus during error processing. Greater symptom reduction correlated with weaker pre-treatment activity across frontoparietal, dorsal attention, visual, and subcortical regions during response inhibition, and stronger default mode activity during error processing. Machine learning models predicted CBT response with modest AUC values of 0.66–0.67, but prediction of remission or using other data types did not exceed chance.
INTERPRETATION: The study leverages a relatively large multi-site sample and uses both mass-univariate and machine learning approaches, strengthening internal validity. However, the modest AUC values indicate limited predictive power at the individual level, and the findings are preliminary without external validation. The heterogeneity in age and imaging protocols across samples may limit generalisability to routine care settings.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current results do not support the use of inhibitory control fMRI activity as a clinically reliable biomarker for predicting CBT outcomes in OCD. Further research with larger, more homogeneous cohorts and prospective validation is needed before considering translation to bedside decision-making.

item.title: Predicting Daily Report Card Treatment Response in Early Childhood ADHD: The Relative Importance of Reward vs. Punishment Sensitivity.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study examined whether reward versus punishment sensitivity in young children with ADHD predicts response to a school-based intervention called the Daily Report Card (DRC) within the Summer Treatment Program for young children (STP-K). The clinical question is whether individual differences in reinforcement sensitivity can guide treatment personalization in early ADHD. The study design was a cohort of 132 children with ADHD (mostly Latinx boys, mean age 5.5 years) assessed before and during a 7–8-week behavioral intervention.
FINDINGS: Children showed higher sensitivity to rewards than punishment at baseline (d = 0.65) and this difference increased during DRC implementation (d = 1.60). Parental adherence to the DRC was high (95%), reinforcement strategies were diverse, and no reward habituation was observed. Pre-treatment reward sensitivity—but not punishment sensitivity—predicted better DRC treatment response.
INTERPRETATION: The study has moderate internal validity with a relatively large, well-characterized cohort and clear behavioral measures, but lacks a control group and randomization, limiting causal inference. The large effect sizes for reward sensitivity and high adherence strengthen confidence in the association, though external validity is limited by the predominantly Latinx, male sample and intensive summer program setting. The lack of punishment sensitivity effect and no habituation data are notable null findings that deserve further study.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These findings support using reward-based DRCs in early ADHD, especially for children with high reward sensitivity, but do not justify abandoning punishment-based strategies entirely. Clinicians should assess reward responsiveness before implementing DRCs and monitor for habituation over time.

item.title: [Deprescribing in geriatric psychiatry: overview of guideline recommendations, deprescribing algorithms, and tools].
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This is a narrative review summarizing guideline recommendations, deprescribing algorithms, and tools for reducing or discontinuing psychotropic medications in older adults with psychiatric disorders. The clinical question is how to safely optimize pharmacotherapy in geriatric psychiatry through deprescribing.
FINDINGS: The review highlights that deprescribing is feasible in most cases and may improve quality of life. It emphasizes the use of potentially inappropriate medication (PIM) lists, guidelines, and deprescribing tools to guide practice. However, individualized risk-benefit assessment and transparent communication with patients and relatives remain essential.
INTERPRETATION: As a narrative review, this paper synthesizes existing guidance rather than presenting new empirical data. Its strength lies in consolidating diverse deprescribing resources, but it lacks quantitative outcomes or head-to-head comparisons. The evidence base is largely derived from guidelines and expert consensus, which may limit generalizability. The clinical recommendations are reasonable but should be applied cautiously, as deprescribing outcomes can vary widely among individuals.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This review supports the integration of deprescribing practices into geriatric psychiatric care but underscores the need for individualized decision-making. Clinicians should use PIM lists and deprescribing tools as aids, while prioritizing patient-centered discussions about risks and benefits.

item.title: French psychiatric caregivers' perceptions of psychedelics: A national survey.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: With France only recently initiating psychedelic trials in 2024, this national online survey examined French psychiatric caregivers’ knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions toward therapeutic and recreational use of psychedelics (LSD, psilocybin, DMT) among 298 respondents (December 2023–January 2024).
FINDINGS: 88% had heard of medical studies, with high awareness of psilocybin and ketamine for treatment-resistant depression. 53% rated the therapeutic benefit-risk ratio as favorable, while 61% viewed recreational use as dangerous. Favorable therapeutic views correlated with male gender, personal psychedelic experience, and ketamine practice; in a subgroup (psychiatrists, residents, nurses), only ketamine practice remained significant. Personal experimentation predicted more positive attitudes toward recreational use.
INTERPRETATION: The study suggests moderate, cautious openness to therapeutic psychedelics among French caregivers, shaped by personal and clinical exposure—especially ketamine. The cross-sectional survey design, modest sample (n=298), and reliance on self-report limit causal inference and generalizability beyond public hospital staff. Findings reflect attitudes at a single time point, before France’s 2024 trials, so future shifts are likely.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current attitudes do not yet justify changes in routine practice, but the strong influence of ketamine exposure implies that early trial participation and education may shape future acceptance among French psychiatric teams.

item.title: Steroidomic Differences Among Clozapine, Olanzapine, and Risperidone in Male Patients with First-Episode Psychosis, Including a Treatment-Resistant Schizophrenia Subgroup.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This pilot cross-sectional study investigated whether clozapine (Clo) produces a distinctive neuroactive steroid (NAS) profile compared with olanzapine (Ola) and risperidone (Ris) in male patients with first-episode psychosis, including a treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS) subgroup receiving Clo. The goal was to explore mechanistic differences that might underlie clozapine’s unique clinical efficacy.
FINDINGS: After 12–18 months of treatment, serum steroidomic profiles were analyzed by GC-MS/MS. Global steroid concentrations did not differ significantly between Clo and Ola (p = 0.515), but multivariate orthogonal partial least squares (OPLS) analysis distinguished Clo from Ola with R²Y = 50.8% and CV-ANOVA p = 0.011. Clo showed lower DHEA, higher 5α-reduced pregnane NAS, altered androgen turnover, reduced CYP17A1 lyase proxy activity, and a mild increase in the cortisol-to-cortisone ratio. Clo was also clearly distinguished from Ris by broad steroid increases. Sample size and follow-up duration were not explicitly stated.
INTERPRETATION: The study’s internal validity is limited by its small, male-only, cross-sectional design and lack of independence among steroid pathways, which increases the risk of spurious associations. While the multivariate separation between Clo and Ola is statistically robust, the clinical meaning remains exploratory. The absence of longitudinal data and adjustment for multiple comparisons further constrains causal inference. The observed steroidomic pattern may reflect neuroprotective or GABAergic modulation, but this is speculative without functional validation.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These preliminary findings do not yet justify changes in antipsychotic selection. They suggest a potential biomarker signal that warrants larger, longitudinal, sex-balanced studies with functional assays to determine whether steroidomic profiles can predict or mediate treatment response.

item.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Incident Cardiovascular Events and Death in Treated Serious Mental Illness, Type 2 Diabetes, and Obesity.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This retrospective propensity score–matched cohort study (n=218 043) in the TriNetX database examined whether glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) reduce incident myocardial infarction (MI), heart failure (HF), and all-cause death over 1 and 3 years in adults with serious mental illness (SMI), type 2 diabetes, and obesity who were receiving antipsychotic or antidepressant treatment.
FINDINGS: GLP-1RA use was associated with lower absolute risk differences at 1 and 3 years: MI −0.7 % and −1.0 %, HF −1.1 % and −1.8 %, and all-cause death −3.9 % and −6.5 % (all P<0.001). Semaglutide or tirzepatide showed similar reductions. Results remained directionally consistent after adjustment for SGLT2 inhibitors and DPP-4 inhibitors.
INTERPRETATION: The large, propensity-matched cohort suggests clinically meaningful reductions in cardiovascular events and mortality with GLP-1RA therapy in this high-risk population. However, residual confounding from unmeasured variables (e.g., lifestyle, adherence, severity of SMI) and reliance on administrative codes limit causal inference. The magnitude of benefit is plausible given known cardiometabolic effects of GLP-1RAs, but replication in prospective trials is needed.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These findings support consideration of GLP-1RAs in patients with SMI, type 2 diabetes, and obesity on psychotropic medications, particularly when cardiometabolic risk is high. Clinicians should weigh benefits against adverse effects and cost while awaiting confirmatory evidence.

item.title: The Early Youth Engagement (EYE-2) Intervention in First Episode Psychosis Services: Definition and Implementation of a Therapeutic Motivational-Engagement Model for Early Intervention in Psychosis Key Workers.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Psychosis is associated with high disability and societal costs. Early Intervention in Psychosis (EIP) services enhance mental health outcomes, but 15% disengage and more engage intermittently. There is no EIP-specific therapeutic model for how Key Workers should maximize engagement. AIMS: To identify factors that define the Early Youth Engagement (EYE) therapeutic model for Key Workers in EIP services and affect implementation. METHODS: The design was a cross-sectional qualitative thematic analysis and the final phase of an iterative mixed-methods model development.

item.title: Phenotypic Complexity and Diagnostic Utility of Exome Sequencing in ASD: Real-World Insights from Colombia.
item.description: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a genetically heterogeneous condition; however, genomic data from Latin American populations remain limited. We investigated the molecular and phenotypic landscape of ASD in 916 Colombian patients who underwent whole-exome sequencing (WES) between 2022 and 2025. Clinical and genomic data were retrospectively analyzed, and phenotypes were standardized using Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms.

item.title: Cord-Derived Stem Cells for Pediatric Autism Spectrum Disorder: Biological Rationale and Source-Specific Trial Design.
item.description: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) affects approximately 1 in 31 children, yet no pharmacological agent targets its core symptoms, leaving a substantial therapeutic gap. Umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (UC-MSCs) have emerged as a biologically rational candidate, because their immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and neurotrophic properties align with the chronic neuroinflammation, peripheral immune dysregulation, and microglial overactivation that characterize ASD pathophysiology.

item.title: Human uniqueness and vulnerability to mental disorder.
item.description: Among all animals, humans stand out as uniquely vulnerable to mental disorder. Explaining this vulnerability constitutes a central challenge for psychiatry that requires an explicitly evolutionary approach. A necessary first step is a rigorous scientific account of human uniqueness: species-specific psychological/behavioural traits distinguishing Homo sapiens from other animals.

item.title: Associations of physical activity bout duration and fragmentation with future dementia, depression, and anxiety: a multi-modal UK Biobank study.
item.description: It's unclear whether prolonged physical activity confers greater benefits on future dementia, depression, and anxiety risk than sporadic activity. Among 66,483 UK Biobank participants, we found that prolonged daily bouts of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) and lower activity fragmentation were associated with a significantly lower risk of future dementia, depression, and anxiety, independent of total physical activity.

item.title: A cross-sectional analysis of topical steroid phobia and observable side effects in Thai psoriasis patients.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Steroid phobia impairs adherence to topical corticosteroids (TCS) and undermines psoriasis management, yet remains understudied in adult Thai patients. OBJECTIVES: To quantify TCS phobia using the TOPICOP scale in Thai adults with psoriasis and identify associated factors. METHODS: A cross-sectional survey at Siriraj Hospital enrolled 150 adults with psoriasis and TCS experience, who completed the validated Thai TOPICOP scale. RESULTS: Of 150 participants, 81 (54.0%) were female, median age 52 years (IQR 35.0-62.3). Mean TOPICOP score was 17.1 ± 5.3/36 (47.5% ± 14.7%).

item.title: Behavioral, Psychological, and Metabolic Characteristics of Adults with Co-Occurring Generalized Anxiety Disorder and Obesity: A Cross-Sectional Study.
item.description: Background: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) and obesity are highly prevalent and often co-occur, yet it remains unclear how the presence of both conditions relates to biological, behavioral, and psychological outcomes compared with either condition alone. Understanding this subgroup is crucial to improving assessments and treatment outcomes. Objective: To characterize biological, psychological, and behavioral parameters among individuals living with obesity (LWO) and GAD (GAD + LWO), compared with those with only one condition (GAD or LWO) and healthy controls.

item.title: A 25-Year Nationwide Analysis of Mortality Trends due to Intentional Self-Harm by Hanging, Strangulation, and Suffocation.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Suffocation, strangulation, and hanging are among the deadly forms of intentional self-harm, which is a serious global public health issue. These types of self-harm frequently have high fatality rates and greatly increase the United States' suicide burden. Analyzing trends over time is essential for noticing evolving patterns, directing preventative measures, and developing successful policy interventions.

item.title: MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction contributes to neuronal hyperexcitability and depressive-like behaviors.
item.description: Astrocyte pathology is increasingly recognized as a key factor in the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD), where disrupted glutamate clearance and impaired neuron-glia interactions contribute to synaptic dysfunction. However, the molecular mechanisms leading to astrocyte loss remain largely undefined. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of MDD, yet most studies have focused on neuronal mitochondria, leaving astrocytic mitochondrial dynamics insufficiently investigated. Here, we identify mitofusin-2 (MFN2)-associated astrocyte dysfunction in depression.

item.title: Fibroblast Growth Factors and Their Receptors in Major Depressive Disorder: A Scoping Review of Translational Research.
item.description: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a complex psychiatric condition whose pathophysiology extends beyond the classic monoamine hypothesis, involving impaired neuroplasticity, neuroinflammation, HPA axis dysregulation, and altered neurotrophic signaling. The fibroblast growth factor (FGF) system, comprising ligands and their receptors (FGFRs), has emerged as a key candidate regulator of these processes. This scoping review qualitatively synthesizes current clinical, postmortem, and preclinical evidence on the role of the FGF system in MDD and antidepressant response.

item.title: Utility of pharmacogenomic tests in treating pediatric depression, anxiety and ADHD.
item.description: Despite the scientific advancement and increasing interest in the use of pharmacogenomic tests to determine how genes interact with medications, such tests require nuanced understanding and interpretation in the treatment of pediatric depression, anxiety, and ADHD. Pharmacogenomic testing can be useful in certain populations to identify a psychotropic medication's tolerability or adverse effects. Pharmacogenomic testing cannot predict which medication will provide the best clinical response in a specific patient with a specific mental illness.

item.title: Eating Behaviors, Dietary Patterns and Diet Quality in Newly Diagnosed, Treatment-Naïve Children with ADHD: An Age- and Sex-Matched Case-Control Study.
item.description: Background/Objectives: Evidence on eating behaviors and dietary characteristics in children with ADHD is limited by clinical heterogeneity and narrow assessment approaches. This exploratory matched case-control study compared eating behaviors, diet quality, highly processed food consumption, and empirically derived dietary patterns between newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve children with ADHD and age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Methods: The study included 64 children with ADHD without major comorbidities and 64 healthy controls individually matched by sex and age (±6 months).

item.title: Beyond Detoxification: The Critical Role of Occupational Therapy in Addiction Clinics.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: This study examines the impact of occupational therapy (OT) activities-such as music, painting and sports-on treatment outcomes for patients with alcohol and substance use disorder treated at the inpatient addiction treatment unit of Sakarya University Training and Research Hospital, in Turkey. The research specifically compares hospitalisation duration and treatment completion rates before and after these activities were discontinued due to regulatory changes.

item.title: Primary Care for People With Alcohol Use Disorder.
item.description: Alcohol use disorder is one of the most common chronic conditions encountered in primary care. In the United States, 1 in 10 people 12 years and older had alcohol use disorder in 2024. Patients with alcohol use disorder have increased risk for complications and comorbidities in gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, and neurologic systems, as well as anxiety and mood disorders, trauma-related stress disorders, suicide, and unintentional injuries.

item.title: National Trends in Sexual Behavior, Substance Use and HIV Testing Among United States Men Who Have Sex With Men Recruited Online, 2017 Through 2024.
item.description: BackgroundGay men and other men who have sex with men are disproportionately impacted by HIV and other sexual transmitted infections. Thus, monitoring changes to HIV-related risk and prevention behaviors are relevant to contextualizing public health programming.

item.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of PID-5-BF for Screening Personality Disorders: A Cross-Sectional Study in Clinical and Nonclinical Samples.
item.description: The DSM-5 Alternative Model for Personality Disorders introduced a dimensional approach to personality pathology, with maladaptive traits assessed by the Personality Inventory for DSM-5 Brief Form (PID-5-BF). Despite extensive validation, evidence on its diagnostic accuracy and empirically derived cutoff scores remains limited. This study aims to compare PID-5-BF trait levels and profiles across individuals with personality disorders (PDs), clinical participants without PDs, and nonclinical participants and to evaluate its diagnostic accuracy and screening cutoffs.

item.title: Body image disturbance and body dysmorphic symptoms among Bangladeshi university students: associated factors and Bayesian network analysis.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Body image disturbance and body dysmorphic symptoms are important appearance-related mental health concerns among university students, yet evidence from Bangladesh remains limited. This study examined factors associated with body image disturbance and body dysmorphic symptoms among Bangladeshi university students and explored their conditional dependency structure using Bayesian network analysis. METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 1,401 residential students at Jahangirnagar University, Bangladesh, between December 2024 and January 2025.

item.title: Schizophrenia-associated gut microbiota are linked to reduced colonic PRODH expression and behavioral changes in mice.
item.description: Schizophrenia (SCZ) is a chronic neuropsychiatric disorder whose biological basis remains incompletely understood. Growing evidence implicates the gut-brain axis in SCZ, but the host pathways through which disease-associated microbiota may influence behavior remain unclear. Here, we examined whether the gut microbiota from patients with SCZ is associated with behavioral and metabolic alterations in male C57BL/6N mice.

item.title: Acoustic Features of Sustained Phonation for Schizophrenia Classification: A Feasibility Study.
item.description: Voice and speech are increasingly studied as indicators of mental health, but the acoustic features of sustained phonation in schizophrenia remain underexplored. This feasibility study examined whether a 500 ms sustained vowel /a/ contains meaningful information for distinguishing patients with schizophrenia from healthy controls. Recordings from 84 participants (41 patients, 43 controls) were analyzed using features from eight acoustic domains.

item.title: Minocycline-Mediated Inhibition of Microglial Activation in Neuroinflammation-Related Neuropsychiatric Disorders: Preclinical Promise and Clinical Limitations.
item.description: Minocycline, a second-generation tetracycline antibiotic, has attracted interest as a CNS-active anti-inflammatory agent because it crosses the blood-brain barrier and inhibits microglial activation. This review summarizes preclinical and clinical evidence for minocycline in neuroinflammation-related neuropsychiatric disorders, focusing on Alzheimer's disease (AD), Lewy body disease (LBD), schizophrenia, and major depressive disorder (MDD).

item.title: Substance Misuse Prevalence and Risk Factors in Adolescents and Young Adults With Depression.
item.description: IMPORTANCE: The prevalence of youths with mental health conditions has increased in recent years. Youths with mental health conditions are at risk of substance misuse via coping and self-regulation pathways; there is therefore a need to identify and address barriers to integrated mental health and substance use treatment in these youths. OBJECTIVE: To examine the prevalence of and motivations for prescription psychotherapeutic drug misuse among youths with and without depression.

item.title: (Un)aware of change? Objective and subjective reactivity to the sensor-based measurement of physical activity and sedentary behaviour.
item.description: OBJECTIVES: Despite being the gold standard for assessing physical activity (PA) under free-living conditions, accelerometer-based assessments are prone to measurement reactivity, that is, changes in people's cognitions, emotions or behaviour due to being measured. Little is known about whether participants are aware of these changes.

item.title: Serum Tau and α-Synuclein in Children With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: Cross-Sectional Associations With Methylphenidate Treatment.
item.description: OBJECTIVE: To compare serum total tau and α-synuclein among controls, drug-naïve children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and children with ADHD receiving methylphenidate. METHODS: Original ELISA spreadsheets provided 26 controls, 29 evaluable drug-naïve participants and 32 methylphenidate-treated participants. Boundary-coded results (> 500 pg/mL for tau; < 938 pg/mL for α-synuclein) were assigned the recorded boundary for rank-based analyses.

item.title: Mental health symptoms and everyday social interaction among university students: an exploratory intensive longitudinal study of relational events within bounded peer networks.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Mental health symptoms are closely linked to social relationships, yet most research examines social connectedness through stable ties or retrospective reports. Less is known about how symptoms are associated with the unfolding micro-dynamics of everyday interaction. This exploratory study examined whether depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, and ADHD symptoms were differentially associated with face-to-face contact and received emotional support among university students.

item.title: Construction of Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) for Triphenyl Phosphate (TPHP)-Induced Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Risk Identification of Neurodevelopmental Toxicity of Aryl Organophosphorus Flame Retardants (OPFRs) Based on Multidimensional Bioinformatic Data.
item.description: Triphenyl phosphate (TPHP) is a widely used plasticizer and organophosphate flame retardant extensively applied in various industrial and consumer products. Due to its pervasive environmental exposure and detection in human samples such as amniotic fluid and breast milk, TPHP has become a pollutant of significant concern in recent years for its potential neurodevelopmental impacts on humans.

item.title: Electrodermal Activity as a Metric of Arousal in Autistic Children Prior to Dental Treatment.
item.description: Several prominent theories have asserted atypical arousal as a biological feature of autism. However, there is mixed evidence regarding atypical arousal patterns, particularly resting-state arousal, in autistic children, with research increasingly using psychophysiological measures, such as electrodermal activity (EDA), to help elucidate arousal levels in individuals who might not otherwise be able to identify such states.

item.title: Case Series: ADHD Phenotype in a Family with NPY Gene Microduplication.
item.description: Background: Neuropeptide Y is a highly conserved neuropeptide involved in several physiological processes, including stress regulation, appetite control, and cognitive functioning. Emerging evidence suggests that alterations in neuropeptide Y signaling may contribute to neurodevelopmental and behavioural phenotypes.

item.title: Placental Insulin-like Growth Factor Signaling and Neurodevelopment: Emerging Evidence from the Placenta-Brain Axis.
item.description: The field of neuroplacentology is a growing area that focuses on the influence of placental function on brain development. This field has expanded our understanding of the placenta's crucial role in proper neurodevelopment as well as placental anomalies that increase the risk of adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes. Neuroplacentology studies have revealed distinct roles of placentally provided hormones and nutrients in neurodevelopment whose disruption by perinatal problems, including inflammation, can increase the risk of neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism spectrum disorder and ADHD.

item.title: Eyes-Open Fronto-Central Alpha Activity as an Electrophysiological Correlate of Working Memory in Children with Predominantly Inattentive ADHD.
item.description: Background/Objectives: This study aimed to identify resting-state quantitative electroencephalography (QEEG) correlates of cognitive performance in children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Methods: ADHD diagnoses were established according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition. Cognitive performance was evaluated using the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children, Fourth Edition, focusing on the Working Memory Index (WMI) and Processing Speed Index (PSI).

item.title: The macroeconomic burden of four alcohol-attributable diseases in China, 1990-2023, and projections to 2030: results from GBD 2023.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Alcohol consumption contributes markedly to the global burden of disease, but macroeconomic assessments of alcohol-attributable diseases in China remain limited. Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) data, this study quantified the macroeconomic burden of four alcohol-attributable diseases in China: alcohol use disorders (AUD), alcoholic cardiomyopathy (ACM), cirrhosis and other chronic liver diseases due to alcohol use (ALD), and liver cancer due to alcohol use (LCA).

item.title: Neonatal abstinence syndrome in Norway - a registry study.
item.description: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Medications and illicit substances taken during pregnancy are transferred to the foetus via the placenta. When the supply ceases after birth, the infant can develop withdrawal symptoms. The aim of the study was to investigate the incidence, neonatal morbidity and regional differences in hospital admissions of infants with neonatal abstinence syndrome (NAS) in Norway.

item.title: Impact of Cannabidiol and Its Synthetic Derivative on Fentanyl Consumption and Fentanyl-Induced Neurometabolic Alterations in Mice.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Opioid use disorder (OUD) remains a critical global health challenge, with highly potent synthetic opioids like fentanyl contributing to overdose deaths. The available treatments have limitations. The endocannabinoid system has emerged steadily as a therapeutic target for the opioid crisis due to its modulatory effects on opioid reward and withdrawal and its involvement in regulating inflammation. These studies investigate the potential of cannabidiol (CBD) and its synthetic derivative (L-1β IN-1) in mitigating fentanyl effects.

item.title: Violent and Nonviolent Suicidal Ideation: Predictors of Suicide Crisis Syndrome Severity in a Longitudinal Study.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Suicide Crisis Syndrome (SCS), an acute cognitive-affective state, has been shown to predict near-term suicidal behaviors, highlighting the need to understand factors associated with its severity. This study examined the relationship between SCS severity and different types of suicidal ideation (violent, nonviolent, and passive). METHODS: 622 adult psychiatric inpatients were assessed at intake, discharge, and one-month post-discharge follow-up.

item.title: Concurrent TMS-EEG to characterise interhemispheric signal propagation over the motor and prefrontal regions: An independent replication of GABAB receptor mechanisms.
item.description: Callosal abnormalities disrupt interhemispheric communications that impair the recovery of a series of neurological and psychiatric disorders. Understanding interhemispheric communication could help identify treatments for disorders with dysfunctional callosal transmission. This study aimed to validate the sensitivity of a TMS-EEG-based measure of interhemispheric signal propagation (ISP) to GABAB receptor modulation, while independently replicating the pharmacological mechanisms of interhemispheric inhibition.

item.title: Dose-dependent efficacy and safety of centanafadine in patients with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: A systematic review of the latest evidence.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review assessed the efficacy and safety of centanafadine, a multimodal norepinephrine-dopamine-serotonin reuptake inhibitor (NDSRI), for ADHD across pediatric, adolescent, and adult populations using randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials. The review synthesized dose-response patterns and adverse events narratively due to heterogeneity in study designs.
FINDINGS: Four RCTs (1,845 participants) were included. In children, high-dose centanafadine significantly improved ADHD-RS-5 scores vs. placebo (-16.3 vs. -10.8; p < 0.001), while low-dose did not (MD -2.7; 95% CI -6.0 to 0.5; p = 0.10). In adolescents, 328.8 mg improved ADHD-RS-5 scores (MD -4.3; p = 0.0006; Cohen’s d = -0.40), but 164.4 mg did not (p = 0.3016). In adults, both 200 mg and 400 mg/day significantly improved AISRS scores (LSMDs -2.74 to -4.42; p ≤ 0.039). Treatment-emergent adverse events ranged from 25%–39% in children, 23.8%–50.3% in adolescents, and 17.6%–31.8% in adults, with higher rates at higher doses in some groups.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence suggests dose-dependent efficacy of centanafadine, particularly in children and adolescents, with smaller but significant effects in adults. However, the review highlights critical limitations: only four RCTs from three publications, short-term follow-up, no active comparators, and potential industry sponsorship bias. The effect sizes (e.g., Cohen’s d = -0.40 in adolescents) are modest and may not translate to clinically meaningful improvements for all patients. The safety profile appears dose-related, warranting caution in dosing.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Centanafadine may offer an additional treatment option for ADHD, but its place in therapy remains uncertain due to limited long-term data and lack of comparative trials. Clinicians should weigh modest efficacy against adverse effects and await further independent, head-to-head studies before considering it a first-line agent.

item.title: Exercise-based interventions for postpartum depressive symptoms: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of exercise modality and weekly volume.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and network meta-analysis examined randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of exercise-based interventions for postpartum depressive symptoms, comparing exercise modalities and weekly volumes using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). The study synthesized evidence to determine whether exercise reduces depressive symptoms and if specific types or doses are more effective.
FINDINGS: Twenty-four RCTs with 1,792 participants (912 intervention, 880 control) were included. Exercise significantly reduced EPDS scores compared to usual care/non-exercise controls (MD = -2.73, 95% CI -3.57 to -1.88; I² = 95%). Yoga/mind-body exercise ranked highest in the exercise-type network (SUCRA = 94.2%), with a modest estimated advantage over aerobic exercise (MD = -2.62, 95% CI -5.16 to -0.08). The 45–90 min/week volume category ranked highest (SUCRA = 84.6%), but no between-volume contrasts were statistically significant. Subgroup analysis suggested shorter interventions (<12 weeks) had larger effects than longer ones (≥12 weeks), but this was exploratory.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence suggests exercise may modestly reduce postpartum depressive symptoms, but high heterogeneity, indirect comparisons, and very low network certainty limit confidence in identifying an optimal exercise type or dose. The star-shaped network and mixed samples (prevention vs. treatment) further constrain conclusions. While exercise may serve as a useful adjunct, it should not replace clinical assessment or indicated treatments like psychotherapy or pharmacotherapy.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Exercise can be considered a low-risk adjunct in postpartum mental health care, particularly for mild symptoms, but clinicians should individualize recommendations and monitor response. The lack of clear dose-response or modality superiority means treatment choices should prioritize patient preference and feasibility over theoretical advantages.

item.title: Ketamine and Esketamine in Acute Suicidal Presentations: Evidence, Limits, and a Conceptual Recovery-Enabling Downstaging Framework.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on intravenous racemic ketamine and intranasal esketamine for acute suicidal presentations in adults, aiming to clarify which outcomes these interventions affect and how they fit into emergency suicide care pathways. It prioritizes randomized trials, meta-analyses, and regulatory documents but does not perform formal risk-of-bias assessment or pooled analysis.
FINDINGS: Intravenous ketamine shows randomized and meta-analytic evidence for short-term reduction in suicidal ideation in selected adults, though effects vary by population, comparator, and follow-up duration. Intranasal esketamine (ASPIRE trials) accelerated improvement in depressive symptoms in hospitalized patients with major depressive disorder and acute suicidal ideation, but did not consistently outperform placebo in reducing suicidality. Neither intervention has evidence for preventing suicide attempts or deaths.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is limited by the lack of formal risk-of-bias assessment and absence of pooled reanalysis, reducing confidence in effect estimates. The short-term nature of observed benefits and lack of impact on hard outcomes (attempts/deaths) constrain clinical utility. The proposed "downstaging framework" is conceptual and unvalidated, offering a theoretical approach rather than evidence-based guidance.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Ketamine/esketamine may offer short-term symptomatic relief in carefully selected patients but should not be viewed as suicide-preventive. They must be integrated into comprehensive emergency care, including safety planning and risk formulation, without replacing standard interventions.
